company.title:
Two regulated stablecoin events landed this week, in two jurisdictions.

Israel's Capital Market Aut
company.description:
Two regulated stablecoin events landed this week, in two jurisdictions.

Israel's Capital Market Authority authorised BILS — the first regulated shekel-pegged stablecoin — issued by Bits of Gold on Solana. Fireblocks custody, EY auditing 1:1 reserves.
---
Then Dubai. Ripple opened its Middle East and Africa HQ in DIFC on 30 April, and the DFSA recognised RLUSD ($1.557B market cap) as an approved crypto token for use by regulated DIFC firms — building on Ripple's March 2025 DFSA payments licence.
---
The pattern under both: a sovereign stablecoin entering the regulated set extends the issuer-side KYC perimeter into a fresh jurisdiction. New issuer, new custodian, new on-chain transfer rules — three layers where compliance attestation now has to live.
---
For CASPs onboarding either token, reusable attestations let identity proofs verified for USDC or EURI travel with the customer — collapsing three document-collection workflows into one. The regulated perimeter is widening faster than per-vendor onboarding scales.
